correctness.rationale: Explicit Euler summation proves odd-block uniform sqrt-X lower bound on each bounded vertical interval. Published Harper Theorem 1 bounds each fixed subcritical H^p norm by sqrt-X/(loglog X)^{1/4}; averaging over prime-2 Bohr variable contracts p>=1. Countable open-dense sets in the complete odd Fréchet intersection yield one F for all intervals and p. Independent prime coordinates give an exact norm product, which makes the embedded disk Fréchet space closed; nonzero analytic disk factors are bounded away from zero on a smaller interval, so local logarithmic mass diverges everywhere. All hypotheses and upper-limit quantifiers appear in RESULT.md. Finite checker is supplemental only.

value.rationale: The question whether a recently proved local Nevanlinna failure is exceptional or structurally prevalent is natural. This result shows robustness under every exponent below the sharp threshold and every critical-boundary interval, then proves the bad class contains a closed infinite-dimensional copy of a canonical Hardy intersection, a much stronger linear-geometric classification than one bad function or residuality alone. The closedness and independent-prime factorization are substantive rather than a routine numerical refinement.
